newsitem.title: ITALY: Consob studies foreign stakes in Olivetti.
newsitem.headline: Consob studies foreign stakes in Olivetti.

text.p: Italy's stock market regulatory body Consob said it was investigating whether foreign investors had taken large stakes in information and technology group Olivetti without informing the necessary authorities.

"It is rightful to mention that at the moment...Consob is checking to see whether large stakes have been bought by foreign institutional investors which were not then revealed," a statement from Consob on Olivetti said.
When someone buys more than a two percent stake in a listed Italian company they have to inform Consob about this.
Consob said that according to its latest files, five groups or individuals held more than two percent of Olivetti.
Carlo De Benedetti, who resigned as Olivetti chairman last month, held 14.53 percent of the firm's ordinary capital.

Chase Nominees Ltd held 5.78 percent of the ordinary capital, Deutscher Auslands Kassenverein AG held 3.84 percent, PDFM Ltd, which is controlled by UBS Asset Management London Ltd, held 3.46 percent and Mediobanca 2.22 percent of the ordinary capital.
